sections.title: Scope
sections.content: Acceptance control plane replaces whole-directory review with immutable changed-set and complete Consumer Closure evidence, deterministic checks, typed routing, and Acceptance-only finalization.

sections.title: Authority
sections.content: VDD owns draft/plan-ready; maintainer owns implementation-authorized and non-authorizing supervised decisions; Quick Dev owns implementation-complete; Acceptance alone owns acceptance-passed. Bootstrap and advisory reviewers produce non-authorizing evidence only.

sections.title: Routing
sections.content: Deterministic checks precede model work. Supervised deterministic-only without triggers requires a current maintainer decision; unattended deterministic-only runs no Bootstrap; focused/full routes run isolated three-role Bootstrap; manual pause is non-authorizing. Registered risks upgrade to full or pause.

sections.title: Evidence And Execution
sections.content: Closure and required-check evidence are identity-bound and stale on candidate or authority change. Segments use immutable descriptors, range-bound source delivery, frozen isolated snapshots, inherited access proof, append-only events, policy-bound progress/watchdog, lease reconciliation, and bounded retry.

sections.title: Validation And Rollout
sections.content: M0 closes runtime recovery and isolation, M1 adds Acceptance strategy, and M2 requires 8-13 regression plus frozen semantic corpus before replacing whole-directory defaults. Cost reduction cannot weaken coverage, authorization, verifier, or semantic-detection parity.
